The PR replaces `(now - started).total_seconds() >= STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` with `elapsed.seconds >= STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` in `_eligible_for_removal`. **Measured** (`get_pr_diff`, `read_repo_file` at head): `STALE_GRACE_SECONDS = 172800` (48h). **Inferred** (Python `timedelta` semantics): `.seconds` is only the sub-day component, always `0 <= seconds < 86400`, and does not include whole days in `.days`. Therefore `elapsed.seconds >= 172800` is never satisfied, so a deregistered subnet never becomes eligible for removal on the grace timer after the change.

Real entry point: `_shrink_allowed` requires `_eligible_for_removal` for every netuid dropped from the prior snapshot (`read_repo_file` head ~297–305). If grace never fires, shrink stays blocked and stale members persist — **poisons-later-row** / **never-expires**.

## Concrete elapsed times (deregistered subnet)

Fix `negative_since = T0`. Compare **base** (`total_seconds()`) vs **head** (`.seconds`). Eligible means `_eligible_for_removal` would return True (ignoring probe/root guards).

| `now - T0` | Base (`total_seconds >= 172800`) | Head (`elapsed.seconds >= 172800`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 23h 59m 59s | Not eligible (86399) | Not eligible (86399) |
| **24h 00m 00s** | Not eligible (86400) | Not eligible (**0** — one full day) |
| **24h 00m 01s** | Not eligible (86401) | Not eligible (**1**) |
| 47h 59m 59s | Not eligible (172799) | Not eligible (86399) |
| **48h 00m 00s** | **Eligible** (172800) | **Not eligible** (**0** — two full days) |
| **48h 00m 01s** | **Eligible** (172801) | **Not eligible** (**1**) |
| 72h | Eligible (259200) | Not eligible (0) |

On both sides of **24h**, base and head agree: still before the 48h policy threshold, so not eligible. On both sides of **48h**, base correctly flips to eligible; head stays not eligible and continues to stay not eligible for arbitrarily long elapsed time because `.seconds` never reaches 172800.

For elapsed **under 24h** within the same UTC day, `.seconds` equals `total_seconds()`, so sub-24h behavior matches; the break appears once elapsed spans one or more whole days.

## Finding

**P0 — grace comparison broken (blocking).** Restore `total_seconds()` (or compare `elapsed >= timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS)`). The title claims simplification but removes day-aware duration.

## Entry point trace (**measured**)

`SubnetUniverseProvider.refresh_once` → `SnapshotBuilder.build` → `_compute_membership` → returned `netuids` feed `UniverseSnapshot.netuids`, `_build_rows`, `get_netuids()`, `get_pump_membership_rows()`, and `load_membership_receipt()` via `get_snapshot()`.

## Adversarial extremes

| Input | Effect | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Key `"0"` in `validity_map` | Excluded from `netuids` (same intent as `snapshot_coverage` using `int(n) > 0` and `membership_scoring_expected` excluding root) | **inferred** aligned with existing scoring receipt |

| Non-numeric key in `validity_map` | `int(k)` raises → refresh path errors | **inferred**; not introduced by this diff (old code also did `int(k)` without guard) |

No path found where this change lets negative rows skip the 48h grace, overflow to `inf`/`NaN`, or persist unreachable membership that later cycles treat as authoritative without going through existing `_hold_prior` / emergency paths.

## Owner rules

Merge/evidence logic in `_merge_sources` is untouched (**measured**). Chain-wins and grace semantics unchanged.

## Settled alignment

Council receipt already treats root separately (`root_netuid_in_membership`, scoring set excludes `int(n) > 0`) (**measured** in `internal/council/snapshot_coverage.py`). Skipping `0` in the published netuid list matches that split.

**P3 / inferred:** `validity_map` may still retain a `"0"` entry while `netuids` omits 0, so meta that compares `len(validity_map)` to `len(netuids)` could skew slightly; consumers keyed on `snap.netuids` are consistent.

Targeted fix for placeholder netuid 0 in the membership list; no blocking never-expires / overflow / abort-cycle / poison-later-row finding under gate definitions.

## Summary

One-line change in `_compute_membership`: derive `netuids` from `validity_map` keys with `if int(k)`, which **measured** excludes key `"0"` (ROOT) while leaving that entry in `validity_map`.

## Findings

### P2 — ROOT drop is treated as an unsafe shrink (MODIFY)

**Measured:** `_compute_membership` still writes `validity_map["0"]` when `ROOT_NETUID` is in `candidates` (lines 336–337, 371–372). The new list comprehension omits `0` from `netuids`.

**Measured:** `refresh_once` publishes only when `_shrink_allowed` passes (lines 724–733). For any `netuid` removed from `prior.netuids` without `build.dropped[netuid]` and `_eligible_for_removal`, shrink is blocked and `_hold_prior` republishes the old snapshot.

**Measured:** `_eligible_for_removal` always returns `False` for `ROOT_NETUID` (lines 271–272).

**Inferred:** A persisted LKG whose `netuids` already contain `0` will produce builds without `0`, fail `_shrink_allowed`, and retain the prior universe indefinitely — so the fix never lands for those workers until manual snapshot intervention. Fresh universes that never listed `0` in `netuids` benefit; migrated ones do not.

**Suggested fix:** Treat ROOT as non-membership for shrink purposes (e.g. ignore `ROOT_NETUID` in the `_shrink_allowed` set difference, or stop inserting ROOT into `validity_map` / `netuids` at the source). Align comment with behavior: this filters **netuid 0**, not generic “placeholder” string keys — non-numeric keys would still **inferred** abort the comprehension via `int(k)`.

### P4 — `validity_map` vs `netuids` skew

**Inferred:** `universe_snapshot_feed_meta` counts all `validity_map` entries but divides by `len(snap.netuids)`; excluding `0` from `netuids` only can skew majority source inference when a root entry remains in the map.

## Adversarial trace (entry: `SnapshotBuilder.build` → `_compute_membership` → `refresh_once`)

Extremes `NaN`/`inf`/`1e308` do not enter this path (**measured** — keys are `str(netuid)` from integer candidates). Malformed non-numeric keys in a hypothetical `validity_map` would still raise in `int(k)` (**inferred**); current loop only writes numeric string keys (**measured**).

## Owner alignment

Unsafe-shrink retention (**measured** in code comments) correctly blocks silent subnet removal; the same guard **inferred** conflicts with intentional ROOT delisting unless ROOT is exempt.

This head replaces the **chain-wins** branch for `probe_positive is False` (with TMC not explicitly false) with a **dispute → stay positive** branch for `tmc_positive is True and probe_positive is False`. ## Findings

### P1 — Definitive chain negative no longer beats TaoMarketCap listing

**Measured:** `get_pr_diff` at `1748ed870dbd1a1e086dc3a611d6528596734001` removes:

```
if probe_positive is False and tmc_positive is not False:
    # Owner rule: the chain wins...
    return "negative", ... negative_since ...
```

and adds:

```
if tmc_positive is True and probe_positive is False:
    return "positive", sources, True, None, False
```

**Measured:** At head, `_merge_sources` returns `validity="positive"`, `disputed=True`, `negative_since=None` for that pair (`read_repo_file` lines 208–210).

**Inferred:** Session contract: *a definitive chain negative beats a TaoMarketCap listing*; failed/timeout/unknown chain reads are not negatives. Here `probe_positive is False` is produced only after a successful registration read (`_registration_probe` returns `{}, False` on non-ok outcome; on success sets `observed[n] = n in registered`). So this branch is the definitive chain-negative case while TMC still lists the netuid — exactly the case the contract says should **not** stay listed on TMC alone.

**Owner rule:** The deleted comment stated chain wins for a complete read that does not list the netuid. This diff explicitly reverses that.

### P1 — Removal clock cleared; member can never age out on chain evidence

**Measured:** `_compute_membership` only records drops when `validity == "negative"` and `_eligible_for_removal` passes (`read_repo_file` ~358–361). `_eligible_for_removal` requires `evidence.probe is not False` to fail early — actually it requires `probe is False` AND `negative_since` set.

**Inferred:** On the new dispute branch, `negative_since` is forced to `None` even if `prior` had started a grace clock. Validity stays `"positive"`, so no drop path runs. A netuid with a definitive chain negative plus TMC listing can remain in `validity_map` indefinitely without ever entering the 48h negative grace — **never-expires** relative to the intended chain-driven removal policy.

### P2 — Downstream membership set still partially respects probe, but validity map poisons later cycles

**Measured:** `observed_members = {n for n in tmc_positive if probe_map.get(n) is not False} | {n for n, v in probe_map.items() if v is True}` — TMC-listed netuids with `probe False` are excluded from the TMC side of `observed_members`.

**Inferred:** Prior members still enter `candidates` and, under the new merge, stay **positive/disputed** with no `negative_since`. Later refresh cycles read that validity back as prior state — **poisons-later-row** for removal eligibility even when chain evidence is consistently negative.

## Extremes (adversarial, inferred)

- Netuid listed on TMC, absent on successful member list read: **was** `negative` + grace; **now** `positive` + `disputed` + `negative_since=None`. No PASS justification under chain-wins contract.
- Failed probe (`probe_val None`): unchanged paths still treat failed read as not undoing prior negative (`probe_positive is None and prior validity negative`) — consistent with contract. This change only affects the definitive `False` case.

## Settled-check

**Guess:** Full locks/docs not available in this fixture listing; the removed in-code owner comment and the session-pinned contract are sufficient to treat chain-wins as settled for this repo.

## Recommendation

Restore chain-wins for `probe_positive is False` with successful read semantics (or equivalent), allowing `negative` + `negative_since` when TMC disagrees. If product wants a **disputed** flag, it must not downgrade a definitive chain negative to `positive` or clear the grace clock.

## Summary

One-line guard change in `reload_from_disk_if_stale`: drop `not payload.get("netuids")` so any JSON object accepted by `UniverseSnapshot.from_dict` can replace the in-memory snapshot when the persist file mtime advances.

## Diff (measured)

- **Before (inferred from patch):** reload ignored disk updates whose top-level `netuids` was missing or falsy (`[]`), keeping the prior in-memory snapshot.
- **After (measured at head):** reload accepts any `dict` payload and calls `from_dict`; only non-dict payloads are rejected.

## Adversarial trace

**Entry point:** `ensure_universe_reader()` → `reload_from_disk_if_stale()` (non-writer / web path). Writers use `refresh_once()` → `_shrink_allowed` before `_publish`.

**Value path:** `payload.get("netuids")` → `from_dict` builds `netuids = tuple(sorted(int(n) for n in payload.get("netuids") or []))` (**measured**). Missing key and `[]` both yield an empty tuple; invalid element types raise and hit the existing `except`, retaining the prior snapshot (**measured**).

**Extremes / float paths:** not in this diff; no new numeric acceptance.

**Shrink / safety:** `_shrink_allowed` never ran on disk reload (**measured**); that predates this PR. The new behavior is specifically to honor worker-persisted snapshots that legitimately have empty membership (`SnapshotBuilder.build` can emit `netuids=()` with `status="degraded"` and message "Membership resolved empty after validation" — **measured**), which `_atomic_persist` may write when status ≠ `emergency_registry`.

**Consumers:**
- `get_lkg_or_emergency()` maps `not snap.netuids` to `emergency_registry(reason="no_usable_snapshot")` (**measured**).
- Phase-1 scoring admission fails closed on `degraded` / `refresh_incomplete` / emergency via `membership_allows_admission` (**measured** in `internal/council/snapshot_coverage.py`).
- `get_pump_membership_rows()` returns `[]` when `snap.rows` empty (**measured**) — consistent with an intentional empty/degraded publish, not silent inheritance of stale rows.

**Cold start asymmetry (inferred, P3):** `_load_initial_snapshot` still requires truthy `payload.get("netuids")`, so a first boot against a persist file with only `[]` still falls through to `emergency_registry`, while a hot reload would apply the empty snapshot. That is a startup vs reload seam, not introduced shrink-on-refresh; aligning initial load is optional follow-up, not a gate blocker for this scoped change.

## Owner / settled

PR title states intent: reload well-formed persisted snapshots including those with empty membership. No owner standing rule in-repo text contradicts trusting worker disk publish on the reader path.

## Verdict rationale

Tried to break the change via empty/missing `netuids`, corrupt types, and downstream cycle poisoning. Reload already trusted worker disk for non-empty lists without `_shrink_allowed`; this PR fixes the case where the worker intentionally persisted empty/degraded membership. Downstream gates fail closed where required. No blocking never-expires / overflow / aborts-cycle / poisons-later-row finding.

## Summary

Single-line change in `reload_from_disk_if_stale`: drop the extra guard `not payload.get("netuids")` so any JSON object dict is passed to `UniverseSnapshot.from_dict`, matching the PR title (reload well-formed persisted snapshots including legitimately empty membership).

## Diff (measured)

At head `6903a334`, `reload_from_disk_if_stale` now accepts any `dict` payload after `json.load`; base required a truthy `netuids` field before calling `from_dict`.

## Adversarial trace (inferred from code at head)

**Entry point:** reader calls `reload_from_disk_if_stale` → `json.load` → `UniverseSnapshot.from_dict(payload)` → swap `_snapshot` under `_write_lock` when mtime advances.

**Consumers:** `from_dict` normalizes `netuids` via `tuple(sorted(int(n) for n in payload.get("netuids") or []))` (**measured** in file). Missing, null, `[]`, or falsey `netuids` becomes an empty tuple with default `status="ok"` unless payload sets otherwise — the behavior the old reload guard blocked.

**Extremes:** Non-integer netuid entries raise during `int(n)`; the surrounding `except Exception` logs and returns the prior in-memory snapshot (**inferred**), so a corrupt list does not publish. `NaN`/non-numeric strings abort the reload path without updating `_snapshot`. Float netuids that `int()` accepts do not overflow membership math on this path (no grace×3600 style multiply here).

**Bootstrap asymmetry (P3, non-blocking):** `_load_initial_snapshot` still requires `isinstance(payload, dict) and payload.get("netuids")` (**measured**), so a process cold-start with only an empty-but-well-formed file still falls through to `emergency_registry`, while a hot reader reload can adopt the same file once mtime moves. That split predates the intent of this one-line fix and does not introduce never-expire, overflow, or unhandled abort on the reload path.

**Shrink / writer guards:** `_shrink_allowed` applies on the writer `refresh_once` path only (**measured**); reader disk reload never did. Allowing empty snapshots via reload aligns with worker-persisted degraded/empty states the builder can already emit (`build` returns empty `UniverseSnapshot` with `status="degraded"` in some branches). No new unguarded writer shrink in this diff.

MODIFY at `2dee2723c015ef610ce36da8c0afdb37aed61c0a`

## SimiBot comment → head (measured from `verdicts.ts` at head)

1. **`collectPinnedVerdicts`** scans timeline comments.
2. **`simibotMcHead(comment)`** (inferred): returns a head only when `user.login === simibot[bot]`, `performedViaGithubApp.id === 5501340`, and the body contains **exactly one** `<!-- mc-verdict:<40-hex> -->` match (`MC_VERDICT_MARKER`). That full SHA is the pinned head.
3. If `simibotMcHead` is set, **`verdictFromComment`** → **`parseVerdictToken`** reads the first non-marker line. For **`PASS`**, **`passTailAllowed(tail)`** must return true or the comment yields **no verdict** (`noteUnparsed`, then `continue`).
4. On success, the gate records `{ reviewer: "mc", verdict, headSha: simibotHead, … }`. The head that counts is **always the marker SHA**, not anything parsed from the PASS tail.

So a SimiBot MC verdict ends up on **`simibotHead`** from the HTML marker; the first-line pointer is shape-checked only, not reconciled to that marker.

## Findings vs pinned PASS pointer rule

| # | Severity | Label | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | P1 | inferred | **No pointer ↔ `mc-verdict` equality check.** If the first line is `PASS at <shaA> …` (or bare `<shaA>`) while the marker names `<shaB>`, `passTailAllowed` can still accept the line and the branch still emits an MC verdict pinned to **shaB**. The pinned rule for this round requires disagreement to **fail closed** (comment counts as **no verdict**). That check is absent in the SimiBot branch. |
| 2 | P2 | inferred | **`SHA_WORD` allows 7–11 hex “pointers”.** `passTailAllowed` uses `/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i`. The pinned rule requires a prefix of **at least 12** hex when not full 40. Seven-character tails can pass the allowlist while `shaClaimedByComment` elsewhere already refuses `<12` abbreviations (measured in same file). |
| 3 | P2 | inferred | **Bare `PASS` with empty tail is accepted.** `passTailAllowed("")` returns true (`i === words.length` with no words). PR title and allowlist comment imply PASS needs a **head pointer and/or signature** after the token; signature-only (`PASS -simibot`) is fine, but a lone `PASS` should not parse. |
| 4 | P3 | inferred | **Prefix pointers are not resolved.** When the tail carries a 12–39 hex word, nothing calls `input.resolveSha` or compares the resolved full SHA to `simibotHead`. The pinned rule says the prefix must **resolve to the head** and match the marker. |

## What improved (measured)

- Replacing **`WITHDRAWN`** regex with **`passTailAllowed`** fail-closes caveat tails (`PASS, but …`) more reliably than negation lists (measured in diff).
- Dedicated **`simibotMcHead`** path before `subnet-review-gate:` markers correctly attributes SimiBot MC comments and pins to the **`mc-verdict`** marker (measured).
- Unparsed SimiBot lines with a verdict word are logged via **`noteUnparsed`** instead of failing silently (measured).

## Requested follow-up

In the SimiBot MC branch (and/or shared PASS tail helper): parse the optional first-line pointer; if present, require full 40 or ≥12 hex, resolve when short, require equality with `simibotHead`; on mismatch, treat as **no verdict**. Require non-empty tail to include at least a signature or valid pointer. Align `SHA_WORD` minimum with 12 for abbreviated pointers.

No subnet-dashboard runtime paths changed; no suite comparison required for this bot-only diff.

class SnapshotBuilder:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        tmc_fetch: Optional[Callable[[], Tuple[Set[int], Dict[int, Dict[str, Any]], bool]]] = None,
        probe_fetch: Optional[
            Callable[[List[int], float], Tuple[Dict[int, Optional[bool]], bool]]
        ] = None,
        probe_budget_seconds: float = 30.0,
    ) -> None:
        self._tmc_fetch = tmc_fetch or _default_tmc_fetch
        self._probe_fetch = probe_fetch
        self._probe_budget_seconds = probe_budget_seconds

    def build(self, prior: Optional[UniverseSnapshot]) -> MembershipBuild:
        prior_map = dict((prior.validity_map if prior else {}) or {})
        tmc_positive, tmc_rows, tmc_complete = self._tmc_fetch()

        prior_members = set(prior.netuids) if prior else set()
        candidates = set(tmc_positive) | prior_members
        if not tmc_complete:
            probe_candidates = list(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
        else:
            candidates |= set(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
            probe_candidates = sorted(candidates)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self._probe_budget_seconds
        if self._probe_fetch is not None:
            probe_map, probe_complete = self._probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline)
        else:
            probe_map, probe_complete = _default_probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline=deadline)

        if not tmc_complete and not probe_complete and not prior_map:
            return MembershipBuild(UniverseSnapshot.emergency_registry(reason="refresh_unresolvable"))

        netuids, validity_map, cap_reached, refresh_incomplete, dropped = _compute_membership(
            prior_members,
            prior_map,
            tmc_positive=tmc_positive,
            tmc_complete=tmc_complete,
            probe_map=probe_map,
            probe_complete=probe_complete,
        )

        if not netuids:
            had_verified_resolution = bool(
                tmc_positive
                or any(v is not None for v in probe_map.values())
                or (prior_map and (tmc_complete or probe_complete))
            )
            if not had_verified_resolution:
                if prior and prior.netuids:
                    retain_status = (
                        "emergency_registry"
                        if prior.status == "emergency_registry"
                        else "degraded"
                    )
                    return MembershipBuild(
                        _hold_prior(prior, retain_status, "Empty membership from sources — retained prior universe")
                    )
                return MembershipBuild(
                    UniverseSnapshot.emergency_registry(
                        "Empty membership from sources — emergency registry fallback",
                        reason="empty_membership",
                    )
                )
            if prior and prior.netuids and refresh_incomplete:
                return MembershipBuild(
                    _hold_prior(prior, "degraded", "Refresh incomplete — retained last-known-good universe")
                )
            return MembershipBuild(
                UniverseSnapshot(
                    netuids=tuple(),
                    rows=tuple(),
                    resolved_at=_now_iso(),
                    status="degraded",
                    degraded=True,
                    validity_map=validity_map,
                    cap_reached=cap_reached,
                    refresh_incomplete=False,
                    message="Membership resolved empty after validation",
                ),
                dropped,
            )

        rows = _build_rows(netuids, tmc_rows)
        degraded = not (tmc_complete and probe_complete) or refresh_incomplete
        status = "degraded" if degraded else "ok"
        snapshot = UniverseSnapshot(
            netuids=tuple(netuids),
            rows=tuple(rows),
            resolved_at=_now_iso(),
            status=status,
            degraded=degraded,
            validity_map=validity_map,
            cap_reached=cap_reached,
            refresh_incomplete=refresh_incomplete,
            message="" if not degraded else "Refresh incomplete or source degraded",
        )
        return MembershipBuild(snapshot, dropped)

Test-only PR: adds two unit tests on `_eligible_for_removal` in `tests/test_subnet_universe.py`, pinning (1) root netuid `0` never eligible regardless of elapsed negative time, and (2) the 48h grace boundary one second before, at, and after `STALE_GRACE_SECONDS`, plus a 25h negative case.

## Measured

- **Production gate** (`internal/subnet_universe.py` at head): `_eligible_for_removal` returns `False` when `netuid == ROOT_NETUID` (0), when `evidence.probe is not False`, when `negative_since` is missing or unparsable, otherwise `(now - started).total_seconds() >= STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` (172800).
- **Callers**: `_compute_membership` drops a negative netuid only when `_eligible_for_removal` is true; `_shrink_allowed` requires the same for every dropped netuid.
- **New tests** use `DropEvidence(tmc=False, probe=False, negative_since=NOW - elapsed)` so they hit the chain-negative removal path. Assertions match helper branches for netuid 0 vs 5 and elapsed 172799 / 172800 / 172801 seconds and 25 hours.
- **Imports**: `STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` already at module scope; inline import of `_eligible_for_removal` matches other private-helper tests in this file.

## Inferred

- Unit tests complement integration grace tests by locking boundary arithmetic without `SnapshotBuilder`. No production change.
- Parse failures on `negative_since` return `False` without raising; root check is first — no **never-expires**, **overflow**, **aborts-cycle**, or **poisons-later-row** path identified in the diff.

## Findings

None blocking.

    )

def test_chain_unregistered_row_leaves_after_grace_even_if_tmc_is_down(universe_tmp):
    old = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS + 60)).isoformat()
    prior = _prior_snapshot([42, 43])
    prior = replace(
        prior,
        validity_map={
            **prior.validity_map,
            "42": _validity_entry(validity="negative", sources=[], negative_since=old),
        },
    )
    builder = SnapshotBuilder(
        tmc_fetch=lambda: (set(), {}, False),
        probe_fetch=lambda netuids, deadline: ({42: False, 43: True}, True),
    )
    assert 42 not in builder.build(prior).snapshot.netuids


def test_failed_chain_read_does_not_undo_a_chain_negative(universe_tmp):
    """A chain-negative netuid that TMC still lists must stay negative, with its grace clock, across a failed chain read."""
    started = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=5)).isoformat()
    prior = _prior_snapshot([42])
    prior = replace(
        prior,
        validity_map={
            "42": _validity_entry(validity="negative", sources=["taomarketcap"], disputed=True, negative_since=started),
        },
    )
    builder = SnapshotBuilder(
        tmc_fetch=lambda: ({42}, {42: {"netuid": 42}}, True),
        probe_fetch=lambda netuids, deadline: ({}, False),
    )
    entry = builder.build(prior).snapshot.validity_map["42"]
    assert entry["validity"] == "negative"
    assert entry["negative_since"] == started


NOW = datetime(2026, 10, 27, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _dropped_since(elapsed: timedelta):
    from internal.subnet_universe import DropEvidence

    return DropEvidence(tmc=False, probe=False, negative_since=(NOW - elapsed).isoformat())


def test_root_is_never_eligible_for_removal_whatever_the_elapsed_time():
    from internal.subnet_universe import _eligible_for_removal

    assert _eligible_for_removal(0, _dropped_since(timedelta(days=30)), NOW) is False
    assert _eligible_for_removal(5, _dropped_since(timedelta(days=30)), NOW) is True


def test_the_48h_grace_boundary_before_at_and_after():
    from internal.subnet_universe import _eligible_for_removal

    just_before = timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS - 1)
    exactly = timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS)
    just_after = timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS + 1)
    assert _eligible_for_removal(5, _dropped_since(just_before), NOW) is False
    assert _eligible_for_removal(5, _dropped_since(exactly), NOW) is True
    assert _eligible_for_removal(5, _dropped_since(just_after), NOW) is True
    assert _eligible_for_removal(5, _dropped_since(timedelta(hours=25)), NOW) is False

def test_cold_start_empty_tmc_emergency_registry_via_provider(universe_tmp, monkeypatch):

def test_tmc_fetch_bypasses_live_subnet_clip(monkeypatch):
    """Universe membership must not inherit live_subnets 75-row clip."""
    live_stub = [{"netuid": i} for i in range(75)]
    tmc_stub = [{"netuid": i} for i in range(130)]
    monkeypatch.setattr("fetchers.taomarketcap.get_all_subnets", lambda: live_stub)
    monkeypatch.setattr("fetchers.taomarketcap._get_all_subnets_tao", lambda: tmc_stub)
    from internal.subnet_universe import _default_tmc_fetch

    netuids, _, complete = _default_tmc_fetch()
    assert complete
    assert len(netuids) == 130
    assert max(netuids) >= 129


def test_build_probes_full_range_when_tmc_complete():
    """TMC-complete refresh probes 0..MAX_NETUIDS-1 for subnets beyond TMC pagination."""
    prior = _prior_snapshot(list(range(75)))
    probed: list[int] = []

    def probe_fetch(netuids, deadline):
        probed.extend(netuids)
        return {n: True for n in netuids if n >= 125}, True

    builder = SnapshotBuilder(
        tmc_fetch=lambda: (set(range(75)), {n: {"netuid": n} for n in range(75)}, True),
        probe_fetch=probe_fetch,
    )
    built = builder.build(prior).snapshot
    assert max(probed) >= MAX_NETUIDS - 1
    assert len(built.netuids) > 75

def test_no_price_on_one_positive_does_not_snapshot_freeze_membership(universe_tmp, monkeypatch):
    """One refresh: confirmed-positive, TMC-absent no_price, new netuid; shrink aged negative.

    Regression for PR #1378: per-netuid no_price must not set snapshot refresh_incomplete or
    force prior-only membership when a new netuid is observed and an unrelated grace-eligible
    negative is individually complete.
    """
    old = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(seconds=STALE_GRACE_SECONDS + 60)).isoformat()
    prior = UniverseSnapshot(
        netuids=(100, 105, 130),
        rows=(
            {"netuid": 100, "name": "SN100"},
            {"netuid": 105, "name": "SN105"},
            {"netuid": 130, "name": "SN130"},
        ),
        resolved_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        status="ok",
        degraded=False,
        validity_map={
            "100": _validity_entry(validity="positive", sources=["taomarketcap", "blockmachine_probe"]),
            "105": _validity_entry(validity="positive", sources=["taomarketcap", "blockmachine_probe"]),
            "130": _validity_entry(
                validity="negative",
                sources=["taomarketcap", "blockmachine_probe"],
                negative_since=old,
            ),
        },
    )
    builder = SnapshotBuilder(
        tmc_fetch=lambda: (
            {100, 201},
            {
                100: {"netuid": 100, "name": "SN100"},
                201: {"netuid": 201, "name": "SN201"},
            },
            True,
        ),
        probe_fetch=lambda netuids, deadline: (
            {100: True, 105: None, 130: False, 201: True},
            True,
        ),
    )
    built = builder.build(prior).snapshot
    assert built.refresh_incomplete is False
    assert built.message != "Refresh incomplete — retained last-known-good universe"
    assert built.netuids != prior.netuids
    assert 100 in built.netuids
    assert 105 in built.netuids
    assert 201 in built.netuids
    assert built.validity_map["105"].get("refresh_incomplete") is True
    assert 130 not in built.netuids

    monkeypatch.setattr("internal.subnet_universe._ci_or_test", lambda: False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("RUN_MODE", "worker")
    provider = SubnetUniverseProvider(persist_file=str(universe_tmp))
    provider.replace_snapshot_for_tests(prior)
    provider.set_builder(builder)
    result = provider.refresh_once()
    assert result.refresh_incomplete is False
    assert result.netuids != prior.netuids
    assert 201 in result.netuids
    assert 105 in result.netuids
    assert 100 in result.netuids
    assert 130 not in result.netuids

        netuids=(201, 202),
        rows=(
            {"netuid": 201, "name": "SN201"},
            {"netuid": 202, "name": "SN202"},

        resolved_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        status="ok",
        degraded=False,
        validity_map={
            "201": _validity_entry(
                validity="negative",
                sources=["taomarketcap", "blockmachine_probe"],
                negative_since=old,
            ),
            "202": _validity_entry(
                validity="negative",
                sources=["taomarketcap", "blockmachine_probe"],
                negative_since=old,

    builder = SnapshotBuilder(

    assert 202 in built.netuids

    """Source-confirmed positive survives missing on-chain price."""
    prior = _prior_snapshot([77])
    builder = SnapshotBuilder(
        tmc_fetch=lambda: ({77}, {77: {"netuid": 77, "name": "SN77"}}, True),
        probe_fetch=lambda netuids, deadline: ({77: None}, True),
    )

**Measured** from head `internal/subnet_universe.py`:

- Fixed text: `subnet_universe removed %d netuid(s) after the 48h grace: `
- `%d`: `len(removed)` (non-negative int).

def test_t6_concurrent_reads_during_write(universe_tmp):
  """Readers never observe torn snapshots during publish."""
  provider = SubnetUniverseProvider(persist_file=str(universe_tmp))
  provider.replace_snapshot_for_tests(_prior_snapshot([1, 2, 3]))
  errors: list[str] = []
  stop = threading.Event()

  def reader() -> None:
      while not stop.is_set():
          snap = provider.get_snapshot()
          netuids = list(snap.netuids)
          if netuids != sorted(netuids):
              errors.append(f"unsorted: {netuids}")
          if len(set(netuids)) != len(netuids):
              errors.append(f"dupes: {netuids}")

  threads = [threading.Thread(target=reader) for _ in range(8)]
  for thread in threads:
      thread.start()
  for idx in range(20):
      provider.replace_snapshot_for_tests(_prior_snapshot(list(range(idx, idx + 5))))
  stop.set()
  for thread in threads:
      thread.join(timeout=2)
  assert not errors

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class UniverseSnapshot:
    netuids: Tuple[int, ...]
    rows: Tuple[Dict[str, Any], ...]
    resolved_at: Optional[str]
    status: str
    degraded: bool
    validity_map: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cap_reached: bool = False
    refresh_incomplete: bool = False
    message: str = ""

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "version": PERSIST_VERSION,
            "netuids": list(self.netuids),
            "rows": list(self.rows),
            "resolved_at": self.resolved_at,
            "status": self.status,
            "degraded": self.degraded,
            "validity_map": self.validity_map,
            "cap_reached": self.cap_reached,
            "refresh_incomplete": self.refresh_incomplete,
            "message": self.message,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> "UniverseSnapshot":
        netuids = tuple(sorted(int(n) for n in payload.get("netuids") or []))
        rows_raw = payload.get("rows") or []
        rows = tuple(dict(row) for row in rows_raw if isinstance(row, dict))
        return cls(
            netuids=netuids,
            rows=rows,
            resolved_at=payload.get("resolved_at"),
            status=str(payload.get("status") or "ok"),
            degraded=bool(payload.get("degraded")),
            validity_map=dict(payload.get("validity_map") or {}),
            cap_reached=bool(payload.get("cap_reached")),
            refresh_incomplete=bool(payload.get("refresh_incomplete")),
            message=str(payload.get("message") or ""),
        )

    @classmethod
    def emergency_registry(
        cls, message: str = "", *, reason: str = "unspecified"
    ) -> "UniverseSnapshot":
        """Registry-only fallback when committed registry rows exist.

        When registry is missing, returns an empty universe with
        ``refresh_incomplete`` — never fabricates netuids 0..74.
        """
        try:
            from internal.metrics import UNIVERSE_EMERGENCY_TOTAL

            UNIVERSE_EMERGENCY_TOTAL.labels(reason=reason).inc()
        except Exception:
            pass
        logger.warning(
            "subnet_universe emergency_registry (reason=%s): %s",
            reason,
            message or "registry-only rows",
        )
        rows = _emergency_rows()
        netuids = tuple(sorted(_netuid_of(row) for row in rows if _netuid_of(row) is not None))
        incomplete = not netuids
        default_message = (
            "Registry missing — membership incomplete"
            if incomplete
            else "Registry emergency fallback — not the full approved universe"
        )
        return cls(
            netuids=netuids,
            rows=tuple(dict(row) for row in rows),
            resolved_at=_now_iso(),
            status="emergency_registry",
            degraded=True,
            validity_map={str(n): _validity_entry(validity="unobserved", sources=["registry"]) for n in netuids},
            refresh_incomplete=incomplete,
            message=message or default_message,
        )


class SnapshotBuilder:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        tmc_fetch: Optional[Callable[[], Tuple[Set[int], Dict[int, Dict[str, Any]], bool]]] = None,
        probe_fetch: Optional[
            Callable[[List[int], float], Tuple[Dict[int, Optional[bool]], bool]]
        ] = None,
        probe_budget_seconds: float = 30.0,
    ) -> None:
        self._tmc_fetch = tmc_fetch or _default_tmc_fetch
        self._probe_fetch = probe_fetch
        self._probe_budget_seconds = probe_budget_seconds

    def build(self, prior: Optional[UniverseSnapshot]) -> MembershipBuild:
        prior_map = dict((prior.validity_map if prior else {}) or {})
        tmc_positive, tmc_rows, tmc_complete = self._tmc_fetch()

        prior_members = set(prior.netuids) if prior else set()
        candidates = set(tmc_positive) | prior_members
        if not tmc_complete:
            probe_candidates = list(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
        else:
            candidates |= set(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
            probe_candidates = sorted(candidates)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self._probe_budget_seconds
        if self._probe_fetch is not None:
            probe_map, probe_complete = self._probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline)
        else:
            probe_map, probe_complete = _default_probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline=deadline)

        if not tmc_complete and not probe_complete and not prior_map:
            return MembershipBuild(UniverseSnapshot.emergency_registry(reason="refresh_unresolvable"))

        netuids, validity_map, cap_reached, refresh_incomplete, dropped = _compute_membership(
            prior_members,
            prior_map,
            tmc_positive=tmc_positive,
            tmc_complete=tmc_complete,
            probe_map=probe_map,
            probe_complete=probe_complete,
        )

        if not netuids:
            had_verified_resolution = bool(
                tmc_positive
                or any(v is not None for v in probe_map.values())
                or (prior_map and (tmc_complete or probe_complete))
            )
            if not had_verified_resolution:
                if prior and prior.netuids:
                    retain_status = (
                        "emergency_registry"
                        if prior.status == "emergency_registry"
                        else "degraded"
                    )
                    return MembershipBuild(
                        _hold_prior(prior, retain_status, "Empty membership from sources — retained prior universe")
                    )
                return MembershipBuild(
                    UniverseSnapshot.emergency_registry(
                        "Empty membership from sources — emergency registry fallback",
                        reason="empty_membership",
                    )
                )
            if prior and prior.netuids and refresh_incomplete:
                return MembershipBuild(
                    _hold_prior(prior, "degraded", "Refresh incomplete — retained last-known-good universe")
                )
            return MembershipBuild(
                UniverseSnapshot(
                    netuids=tuple(),
                    rows=tuple(),
                    resolved_at=_now_iso(),
                    status="degraded",
                    degraded=True,
                    validity_map=validity_map,
                    cap_reached=cap_reached,
                    refresh_incomplete=False,
                    message="Membership resolved empty after validation",
                ),
                dropped,
            )

        rows = _build_rows(netuids, tmc_rows)
        degraded = not (tmc_complete and probe_complete) or refresh_incomplete
        status = "degraded" if degraded else "ok"
        snapshot = UniverseSnapshot(
            netuids=tuple(netuids),
            rows=tuple(rows),
            resolved_at=_now_iso(),
            status=status,
            degraded=degraded,
            validity_map=validity_map,
            cap_reached=cap_reached,
            refresh_incomplete=refresh_incomplete,
            message="" if not degraded else "Refresh incomplete or source degraded",
        )
        return MembershipBuild(snapshot, dropped)

def test_t1_empty_state_emergency_registry(universe_tmp):
  """Cold boot with no disk file serves emergency_registry.

  Missing gitignored registry ⇒ empty netuids, refresh_incomplete (no synthetic 0..74).

  provider = SubnetUniverseProvider(persist_file=str(universe_tmp))

  assert snap.degraded is True
  assert len(snap.netuids) == 0
  assert snap.refresh_incomplete is True
  emergency = provider.get_lkg_or_emergency()
  assert emergency.status == "emergency_registry"
  assert len(emergency.netuids) == 0

      tmc_fetch=lambda: ({1, 2, 3}, {1: {"netuid": 1}, 2: {"netuid": 2}, 3: {"netuid": 3}}, True),
      probe_fetch=lambda netuids, deadline: ({n: True for n in netuids}, True),
  ).build(None).snapshot
  assert built.status == "ok"
  assert len(built.netuids) == MAX_NETUIDS
  assert built.netuids[:4] == (0, 1, 2, 3)

        netuids=tuple(netuids),
        rows=rows,
        resolved_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        status="ok",
        degraded=False,

## Summary

This PR removes two GitHub reads on the tag and verdict post paths: `isStale` before slot tags in `postSlotOnce`, and the immediate `alreadyPosted` re-read (guard 3) plus `lostToRecheck` handling in `postVerdictComment`. The motivation (fewer round trips under multi-process, no KV CAS) is clear, but the diff deletes protections that the surrounding comments still treat as load-bearing, without replacing them or updating those comments.

## Findings

### P2 — Stale slot tags after push or draft flip (`postSlotOnce`)

**Inferred** from the diff and head `tag.ts`: `postSlotOnce` no longer calls `isStale` immediately before `postComment`. The `superseded` flag is never set in that path anymore, so `tagOutcome`'s stale branch is dead for tags.

**Inferred** race: Process A reads gate at head `H1`, takes the KV lease, and a push lands to `H2` (or the PR turns draft) while the post is in flight. Without a last-moment `pulls.get`, A still posts `@cursor review` / `@replit review` with a marker for `H1`. The in-file doc on `isStale` (lines 57–62) still explains that this is exactly what the pre-write stale check prevented. Reviewers can be pinged for a head that is no longer the PR tip.

### P2 — Wider duplicate MC verdict window (`postVerdictComment`)

**Measured** in head `lock.ts`: hosted KV is plain get/put without CAS (`supportsKvCas` false); cross-process posting is documented as at-most-once best effort.

**Inferred** from removed guard 3: two processes can both pass the initial `alreadyDone()` in `ranOnceExclusive`, contend on `claim`, and the winner's `run()` no longer re-reads comments adjacent to `createComment`. A loser that still enters `run()`, or two winners in the documented no-CAS edge, can emit two bot-owned `mc-verdict` markers for the same head with different bodies.

**Inferred** from head `gate.ts` `verdictAt`: multiple MC verdicts at one head leave the **last** one in comment order as authoritative. A duplicate post can change which PASS/MODIFY/FAIL the gate believes without a new review turn—state the removed `lostToRecheck` path explicitly treated as "the other comment wins, this is a no-op."

`isStale` remains before the verdict write (good); only the comment re-read and its outcome mapping were removed.

### P3 — Documentation still describes guard 3 and immediate re-read

**Measured** on head after this diff:

- `postVerdictComment` JSDoc still lists three guards and says guard 3 re-reads comments immediately before the post (lines 214–227).
- Module header still says `postVerdictComment` re-reads immediately before posting (lines 36–38).
- `lock.ts` still says callers re-read immediately before posting and names `postVerdictComment` (lines 28–29).

Head code no longer performs that re-read. Readers will underestimate duplicate-post and stale-tag risk.

## What would unblock PASS

1. Restore `isStale` in `postSlotOnce` immediately before `postComment` (one read per tag write), **or** an equivalent single pre-write check that sets `superseded` the way `tagOutcome` already handles.
2. Restore the adjacent `alreadyPosted` check before verdict `createComment`, **or** explicitly accept duplicate verdict comments and rewrite the three guard docs plus `lock.ts` to match (including how the gate picks among duplicates).
3. Align all stale comments with whatever behavior ships.

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> "UniverseSnapshot":
        netuids = tuple(sorted(int(n) for n in payload.get("netuids") or []))
        rows_raw = payload.get("rows") or []
        rows = tuple(dict(row) for row in rows_raw if isinstance(row, dict))
        return cls(

            rows=rows,
            resolved_at=payload.get("resolved_at"),
            status=str(payload.get("status") or "ok"),

            refresh_incomplete=bool(payload.get("refresh_incomplete")),
            message=str(payload.get("message") or ""),
        )

    @classmethod
    def emergency_registry(
        cls, message: str = "", *, reason: str = "unspecified"
    ) -> "UniverseSnapshot":
        """Registry-only fallback when committed registry rows exist.

        When registry is missing, returns an empty universe with
        ``refresh_incomplete`` — never fabricates netuids 0..74.

        try:

    def __init__(
        self,

        tmc_fetch: Optional[Callable[[], Tuple[Set[int], Dict[int, Dict[str, Any]], bool]]] = None,
        probe_fetch: Optional[
            Callable[[List[int], float], Tuple[Dict[int, Optional[bool]], bool]]
        ] = None,
        probe_budget_seconds: float = 30.0,
    ) -> None:
        self._tmc_fetch = tmc_fetch or _default_tmc_fetch
        self._probe_fetch = probe_fetch
        self._probe_budget_seconds = probe_budget_seconds

    def build(self, prior: Optional[UniverseSnapshot]) -> MembershipBuild:
        prior_map = dict((prior.validity_map if prior else {}) or {})
        tmc_positive, tmc_rows, tmc_complete = self._tmc_fetch()

        prior_members = set(prior.netuids) if prior else set()
        candidates = set(tmc_positive) | prior_members
        if not tmc_complete:
            probe_candidates = list(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
        else:
            candidates |= set(range(MAX_NETUIDS))
            probe_candidates = sorted(candidates)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self._probe_budget_seconds
        if self._probe_fetch is not None:
            probe_map, probe_complete = self._probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline)
        else:
            probe_map, probe_complete = _default_probe_fetch(probe_candidates, deadline=deadline)

        if not tmc_complete and not probe_complete and not prior_map:
            return MembershipBuild(UniverseSnapshot.emergency_registry(reason="refresh_unresolvable"))

        netuids, validity_map, cap_reached, refresh_incomplete, dropped = _compute_membership(
            prior_members,
            prior_map,
            tmc_positive=tmc_positive,
            tmc_complete=tmc_complete,
            probe_map=probe_map,
            probe_complete=probe_complete,
        )

        if not netuids:

                or (prior_map and (tmc_complete or probe_complete))

                    return MembershipBuild(

                return MembershipBuild(

                )
            if prior and prior.netuids and refresh_incomplete:
                return MembershipBuild(
                    _hold_prior(prior, "degraded", "Refresh incomplete — retained last-known-good universe")
                )
            return MembershipBuild(
                UniverseSnapshot(

                    rows=tuple(),
                    resolved_at=_now_iso(),
                    status="degraded",
                    degraded=True,
                    validity_map=validity_map,
                    cap_reached=cap_reached,
                    refresh_incomplete=False,

        rows = _build_rows(netuids, tmc_rows)
        degraded = not (tmc_complete and probe_complete) or refresh_incomplete
        status = "degraded" if degraded else "ok"
        snapshot = UniverseSnapshot(

            validity_map=validity_map,
            cap_reached=cap_reached,
            refresh_incomplete=refresh_incomplete,
            message="" if not degraded else "Refresh incomplete or source degraded",
        )
        return MembershipBuild(snapshot, dropped)

## Summary

Single hunk in `_compute_membership`: when `probe_complete` is false and a candidate netuid is missing from `probe_map`, `probe_val` becomes **`False`** instead of **`None`** (measured: `get_pr_diff` at `7b1b5685`).

That value is passed into `_merge_sources` as `probe_positive`. For a prior member still listed by a complete TMC read (`tmc_positive is True`), the branch at lines 210–216 runs (measured: `read_repo_file` `internal/subnet_universe.py` 193–216): validity **`negative`**, **`negative_since`** set to this cycle’s `_now_iso()` when absent from prior. That is a **deregistration clock**, not “nothing observed.”

The pinned contract (2) requires: on chain read failure/timeout, retain last-good membership **and validity**, and **no member gets a deregistration clock**. This head contradicts that for every prior member absent from an empty/failed `probe_map` while TMC still reports them.

`_merge_sources` explicitly preserves grace across failed reads only when `probe_positive is None` (measured: lines 221–223). Forcing `False` bypasses that guard.

## Cycle 2 at the three pinned times (inferred)

Setup assumed from pins: cycle **1** at **T0** with chain read failing (`probe_complete=False`, empty `probe_map`); prior universe already contains the netuid (e.g. from an earlier good refresh); grace **48h**, removal when `(now - negative_since).total_seconds() >= STALE_GRACE_SECONDS` (measured: `STALE_GRACE_SECONDS = 172800`, `_eligible_for_removal` ~268–279).

After cycle **1** at T0 on this head, the affected member gets **`negative_since = T0`** (inferred from merge branch above). Cycle **2** re-runs `_compute_membership` with chain still failing (same `probe_val=False` injection) and fixed `now`:

| Cycle 2 `now` | Effect on affected member |
| --- | --- |
| **T0 + 47h59m59s** | Still **negative**, grace **not** met (`47h59m59s < 48h`); **not** in `dropped`; **remains in `netuids` / membership**; `negative_since` stays **T0**. |
| **T0 + 48h00m00s** | Grace met (`>= 48h`); `_eligible_for_removal` true; netuid in **`dropped`**, removed from **`validity_map`** → **out of membership** for this build (inferred). |
| **T0 + 49h** | Same as 48h: **removed** from membership (inferred). |

If refresh goes through `refresh_once`, `_shrink_allowed` should allow that shrink when evidence is eligible (measured: `_shrink_allowed` + `_eligible_for_removal`).

Under **base** behavior (`probe_val = None` on incomplete missing keys), cycle 1 would **not** start `negative_since` on probe failure (measured: lines 248–256 retain prior positive/unobserved with `refresh_incomplete`); cycle 2 at all three times would **keep** the member with **no new clock** — matching pin (2).

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Label | Finding |
